forecasts.reason: The diagnostic changes no recipe, so the tip's numbers repeat. Profile findings are unmeasured here; small-map layers probably have lower efficiency, but I distrust this without data.
Epoch trims save about 5% per 0.5 epoch and cost 0-0.15 pp. On a tip that sits at 0.754, it is a coin flip whether the bar is cleared.
Group 1 backward is skipped for the last 25% of steps, saving perhaps 3-5%. The accuracy effect is untested, and the added graph variant adds complexity.
Fewer steps cut time, similar to an epoch trim. Dropping easy examples at high label smoothing is unmeasured and may cost accuracy.
The run is compute-bound, so a larger batch saves only a little. 20% fewer steps probably costs some accuracy, and memory is a risk.
Muon lr has been flat (E014). The change is time-neutral, and any accuracy shift is within the noise.

cruxes: What is the tip's true held-out 10-seed mean? If it is at or below 0.752, every further trim fails the bar, and the right move is to buy accuracy back rather than cut time.
Is the run compute-bound at every resolution? If it is, only FLOP and step cuts pay, and batch-size and systems levers are worth about 1% or less.
Does the accuracy cost of each trim add up across trims? Resolution, epoch and width cuts may interact, so each cut costing 0.1 pp alone could cost far more together.
